text:
I made the book like this:

Moaning, weeping, dreaming, ah me.


Sad butterfly, cruel lioness,

I gave lights and shadow all at once.

When I was lioness I never remembered

How one day I could have been butterfly.

When butterfly I never thought

That one day I could set sail or bite.


Shrunken at times and then by leaps

They bled my life and I killed with blood.

Whether now dove, heavy cypress.

Or flowering thicket, I wept and wept more.

Now tasting salts, now tasting honey,

The eyes wept beyond their strength.

Then it matters the same, for I have seen it well,

To be rose or thorn, to be nectar or gall.


Thus I go by curves with my bad thirst

Pruning gardens of every sort.

translation.title: Thus
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the shifting self-figures of butterfly, lioness, dove, cypress, rose, and thorn.
